Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@healthsync.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Classifying Redwood for HealthSync migration window

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We have an upcoming user migration (data import + short-term parsing) scheduled the first two weeks of August. Our legal team is asking whether Redwood can sign an addendum that treats Redwood strictly as a "service provider"/"processor" under CCPA/CPRA for the duration of the migration window and for an agreed 90-day retention period after migration. Specifically they want:

- A commitment that any temporary subprocessor we enable (a partner we use for file ingestion) will only process HealthSync data for the migration task and for no other purpose.
- Written confirmation that no sale or onward sale will occur during or after ingestion (limited use only).
- Evidence of an onshore fallback plan if the temporary subprocessor requires offshoring during troubleshooting.

I've attached the redline the procurement team prepared (healthsync_redline_DPA_v1.pdf) and a short telemetry spreadsheet they want filled out. Can Redwood confirm whether this classification and temporary subprocessor model is acceptable, and whether you can sign an addendum on short notice? Our target go-live for ingestion is Aug 3–7.

Appreciate a quick confirmation,

—Samantha
Samantha Park

Rishi — thanks for the ping. High-level legal position: we can accept a processor/service provider posture and a temporary subprocessor so long as the following are captured in the addendum (we should offer a single-sheet addendum, not rework the full DPA):

1) Limited purpose language: the subprocessor may only process HealthSync data for the ingestion task described in Exhibit A (we will ask Sam to provide a brief scope statement).
2) Timebox: subprocessor access limited to Aug 3–7 plus a 90-day retention period for any ingress artifacts, after which Redwood will delete or expunge ephemeral files per our retention policy. We will propose a 120-hour grace for emergency debug access during the window (with audit logging).
3) No-sale covenant: explicit statement that Redwood will not sell or monetize HealthSync data; limited use only.
4) Onshore fallback: we cannot guarantee full-time onshore support for all third-party partners, but we will provide an onshore fallback process: if the partner indicates offshore-only troubleshooting, Redwood will (a) attempt to re-run ingestion via a Redwood-managed onshore fallback process within 48 hours or (b) provide a documented escalation and audit trail.
4a) For HealthSync, we should offer a short attestation that the temporary subprocessor will not initiate cross-border transfers without notice and written approval.
5) Evidence: provide SOC 2 report and a short telemetry schema (Jonas, can you fill the csv) and a brief description of how we log prefix/KV caching and ephemeral storage during ingestion.

I'll draft the addendum language and a short email to Sam to get the partner legal entity. If Security signs off on the fallback mechanism we can turn this in 48 hours.

—Ben
Ben Carter

Quick technical note and attachments: I populated the telemetry_schema.csv (attached) and added a short technical attestation we can offer in the addendum:

- Telemetry kept minimal: ingestion logs contain request id, timestamp, byte-count, and error-class. No customer content is retained outside of the ingestion buffer.
- KV/prefix caching is ephemeral and flushed immediately after successful ingestion checksum and confirmation from HealthSync (we can add a 90-day retention toggle to match their ask).
- Onshore fallback option: we can spin up a Redwood-managed onshore task using our dedicated pool to re-run ingestion if partner accesses are routed offshore. That process requires a signed addendum and an on-call fee if invoked outside normal SLAs.

Attachments: telemetry_schema.csv

Let me know if the legal language should be more prescriptive around debug access. I recommended an audit-logging requirement and a short notification window (24 hours) for any subprocessor cross-border steps.
